Transjordan
tranz-JOR-duhn
noun (a place)
From Latin trans, across or beyond, and Jordan, the river; the land lying beyond, that is east of, the Jordan; in Hebrew ever ha-Yarden, the side of the Jordan.

📖 Biblical Definition

Transjordan is the region lying east of the river Jordan, the inheritance granted to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh. When Israel came up out of the wilderness, these tribes, having much cattle, saw that the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead were good for cattle, and asked Moses for their portion on the eastern side rather than across the river (Num 32:1-5). Moses granted it on the condition that their armed men cross over and fight for their brethren until the western conquest was complete (Num 32:20-22). The region embraced Gilead and Bashan, the high pastures and the kingdoms of Sihon and Og. After the conquest, as the eastern tribes returned home, they built a great altar by the Jordan; the western tribes feared apostasy and gathered for war, but the altar proved to be a witness, named Ed, that the eastern tribes had part in the LORD (Josh 22:34). This dictionary confesses that the land and its boundaries were the LORD's allotment, and that the altar of witness teaches the unity of the covenant people across every dividing river.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The region east of the Jordan, the inheritance of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, embracing Gilead and Bashan. It is the home of the eastern tribes and of the altar of witness named Ed.

expand to see more

TRANSJORDAN, noun. The territory lying east of the river Jordan, beyond the river from the land of Canaan proper.

It was given to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and embraced the regions of Gilead and Bashan.

"The land which the LORD smote before the congregation of Israel, is a land for cattle, and thy servants have cattle" (Num 32:4).

Its grant required the eastern tribes to cross over armed and fight for their brethren, and forbade them to settle until the conquest was done.

Its closing sense is the altar Ed, a witness that the eastern tribes shared in the LORD with all Israel.

📖 Key Scripture

Num 32:1 — "Now the children of Reuben and the children of Gad had a very great multitude of cattle: and when they saw the land of Jazer, and the land of Gilead, that, behold, the place was a place for cattle;"

Num 32:33 — "And Moses gave unto them, even to the children of Gad, and to the children of Reuben, and unto half the tribe of Manasseh the son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land, with the cities thereof in the coasts, even the cities of the country round about."

Josh 22:10 — "And when they came unto the borders of Jordan, that are in the land of Canaan, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh built there an altar by Jordan, a great altar to see to."

Josh 22:34 — "And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar Ed: for it shall be a witness between us that the LORD is God."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition; the truth to recover is the LORD's sovereign allotment of the land and the unity of His people across every dividing boundary.

expand to see more

Transjordan draws little modern controversy of doctrine, though critical readers treat the tribal allotments as late inventions read back into an idealized past. Scripture presents them as the real grant of Moses and the real conquest under Joshua, the LORD apportioning the inheritance as He had sworn to the fathers. The boundaries east of the Jordan were no less His gift than those to the west.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the unity of the covenant people. The eastern tribes, separated by the river, feared they might be cut off from the LORD's portion; the altar named Ed answered that fear, a witness that those across the Jordan shared in the same God and the same covenant. No river divides the people whom God has joined in His covenant.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From Latin trans (across) and Jordan, the land east of the river; in Hebrew the side or region beyond the Jordan.

expand to see more

Trans, Latin, across or beyond, prefixed to the name of the river.

Yarden, the Jordan, the river descending from the north into the Salt Sea.

Gilead, the mountainous and well-watered region east of the river, good for cattle.

Bashan, the fertile northern land, the kingdom of Og, given to the half-tribe of Manasseh.

Ed, the altar of witness, declaring that the eastern tribes had part in the LORD.

Usage

"The half-tribe of Manasseh received its inheritance in Transjordan, among the heights of Bashan."

"He traced the boundaries of Transjordan from Gilead in the south to Bashan in the north."

"The altar of witness in Transjordan kept the eastern tribes joined to the worship of the LORD."
